title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is section (5) of a 1981-83 'Teichmülleries' note. The isomorphisms (40) identify the group Π_{0,3}^{D_3,τ} with GL(2,Z)/±1 and its relatives. Here they are interpreted 'cartographically', as equivalences of isotopy categories of maps.

The objects:
- Triangular maps X: maps all of whose faces have order dividing 3, i.e. triangles or monogons. In modern terms these are finite-index subgroups (or transitive sets) of PSL(2,Z) = C2*C3. Faces correspond to the order-3 elliptic points, edge midpoints to the order-2 points, and vertices to cusps.
- Weighted ('pondérées') triangular maps X': each vertex carries a weight in {0,1,∞}, and each triangle has its three vertices weighted 0, 1, ∞. These are pullbacks of the standard two-triangle triangulation of P^1 (real line through 0, 1, ∞) under a Belyi map. They correspond to subgroups of Γ(2)/±1, the free group π1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).
- X' is equipped with an action of S_3 that permutes the weights according to the action of S_3 on {0,1,∞}.

The equivalence, valid in both the oriented and unoriented theories:
- Forward direction: X' goes to X = X'/S_3 with the quotient triangulation. The quotient map is ramified at face centres (index 3), edge midpoints (index 2) and vertices (index 2, the stabiliser of a weight being a transposition). This mirrors the degree-6 map λ ↦ j, P^1_λ → P^1_λ/S_3, ramified over 0, 1728 and ∞. Group-theoretically it is Galois theory for the normal subgroup Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z) with quotient PSL(2,F_2) ≅ S_3.
- Inverse direction: start from an ordinary triangulation X and take its barycentric subdivision, whose small triangles are the flags. Define an S_3-principal ramified covering combinatorially by its 'value' on each flag. A flag is read as a weighting of the face containing it, i.e. a bijection of that face's vertices with {0,1,∞}. Gluing across adjacent flags is via the transpositions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞. The result is a ramified principal S_3-covering X' → X on which the pulled-back triangulation is canonically weighted.

On the next page Grothendieck refines this. For a strict triangulation (no monogons, no folded edges), X' is ramified only at vertices of odd degree. When all degrees are even, X' is an unramified S_3-torsor, and its sections correspond bijectively to weightings, i.e. proper 3-colourings of the vertices of X. The sign map S_3 → ±1 gives the associated double cover, whose sections are face 2-colourings: a bipartite dual, a necessary condition in the oriented case.

Purpose: a combinatorial or topological model of the passage between level 1 and level 2 (PSL2(Z) versus Γ(2)), used to interpret the elements ρ, σ_i, τ_i etc. of the Teichmüller-type groups as elements of GL(2,Z)/±1.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. Ramification at vertices of X is stated without qualification; the next page correctly refines it to vertices of odd degree for strict triangulations. In the non-strict case (monogons, folded edges) the local analysis is only sketched.

'Sections ↔ weightings' (next page) holds once all vertex degrees are even and the covering is unramified. Existence of a section is a global condition: the S_3-torsor must be trivial, i.e. have trivial monodromy. Even degrees suffice on the sphere (simply connected) but not in general; Grothendieck's wording leaves this implicit.

ideas.what: Equivalence between triangular maps and {0,1,∞}-weighted triangular maps with an S_3 action permuting weights, via X ↦ X'/S_3, ramified of orders 3, 2, 2 at faces, edges and vertices
ideas.modern_name: Galois correspondence for Γ(2)/±1 ⊲ PSL(2,Z) with quotient S_3; the λ ↦ j covering; hypermaps (Belyi pairs) versus maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical modular-function theory; maps and hypermaps via permutation groups: Jones–Singerman 1978, Walsh 1975
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) treats cartographic groups, triangulations and dessins, but not this explicit S_3 equivalence as far as I know

ideas.what: Reconstructing the S_3-torsor from the barycentric subdivision: flags are local weightings, and adjacent flags are glued by the transpositions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Flag / cartographic-group description of maps; monodromy of a flag torsor
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme, §3 (cartographic groups via flags and barycentric subdivision)

ideas.what: Obstruction to 3-colouring the vertices of a triangulated surface as an S_3-principal covering: ramified at odd-degree vertices, otherwise a torsor whose sections are the 3-colourings; the sign map gives face 2-colourings
ideas.modern_name: Group of projectivities / monodromy criterion for 3-colourability (Heawood's even-degree criterion on the sphere)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heawood 1898 (sphere); Fisk (1970s, geometric colouring theory); Joswig 2002 and Izmestiev–Joswig 2003 (group of projectivities)

missed.claim: Around 1981-82 Grothendieck interprets vertex 3-colourability of a triangulated surface as triviality of a canonical S_3-torsor built from flags, with ramification exactly at odd-degree vertices, i.e. as the level-2 cover Γ(2) ⊂ PSL(2,Z). This anticipates in substance the 'group of projectivities' criterion of Joswig (2002) and Izmestiev–Joswig. It ties that criterion explicitly to the modular tower λ ↦ j and to dessins d'enfants, a link the colouring literature does not usually make.
missed.quote: définit un revêtement principal par sa "valeur" sur chaque drapeau ... ainsi un revêtement ramifié principal X' de X, de groupe S_3, suivant lequel l'image inverse de la triangulation de départ [est naturellement pondérée]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links combinatorial colouring theory (projectivities, Heawood-type criteria) to Belyi maps and level structures. This suggests analogous criteria for other level-N covers, e.g. via n-polygon groups, which the previous page hints at.

deep.surprise_reason: The core equivalence is the well-known Γ(2) ⊂ PSL(2,Z) Galois correspondence in map language. The flag-torsor viewpoint on 3-colourability is a nice early anticipation of later work, but it is mathematically elementary and close to the classical (Heawood/Fisk) picture.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'sur la catégorie des pondérations adjacentes' is more plausibly 'sur la carte [X'] ... sous-jacente'. The S_3 acts on the weighted map X', 'échangeant les pondérations'.

'on trouve une passage au quotient' should read roughly 'on trouve un passage au quotient avec ramification, de plus, aux centres des faces (ramification d'indice 3), des milieux des arêtes (ramification d'indice 2), et [aux] sommets'.

Around 'à l'aide des sommets du groupe S_3' the sense is that one defines, using the group S_3, a principal covering 'défini combinatoirement par sa "valeur" sur chaque drapeau'. Each flag is interpreted as one of the principal flags of the face containing it, giving a weighting of that face.
'[-...-] τ_0(r), τ_1(r), τ_∞(r) [-...-] τ_0,τ_1,τ_∞' should read: passage from one flag to the adjacent flags by τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ (the 'τ_i(r)' phrasing is struck through or overwritten).
Left margins are mostly illegible. The lower margin note appears to concern ramification 'aux centres des faces ... pour ... triangulation' and the conditions on vertices.
